sources.title: Historical Basemaps: Afghanistan record and dated geometry
sources.note: Local indexed record and decoded world-1783 through world-2010 geometry; see identities.json. Open-ended record, last geometry ends 2020. Not a historical authority for sovereignty.

sources.title: Christine Noelle-Karimi, Historiography xi. Afghanistan, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Published 2004; sections 1 and 2. Directly read. Early state formation and Persian historical writing; first two Siraj volumes dated 1331 AH/1912 in article, a lunar year overlapping 1912 and 1913. Public copy uses early 1910s.

sources.title: Daniel Balland, Afghanistan x. Political History, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Published 1983. Directly read Ahmad Shah and Abdur Rahman/Habibullah sections. Used for historically bounded claims, not current politics.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Country Profile: Afghanistan, August 2008
sources.note: Printed pages 2 to 4. Direct PDF extraction. Chronology only; do not reuse erroneous Safavid label for Nadir Shah or Pakistan 1948 date, or obsolete current-country statistics.

sources.title: Clayton Thomas, Afghanistan: Background and U.S. Policy In Brief, March 7, 2025
sources.note: CRS R45122 version 67, printed page 1, Background: Taliban Takeover. Direct PDF extraction. Used only for 2001 to 2021 sequence, not its now-outdated recognition statement.

sources.title: Fayz Muhammad, Siraj al-Tawarikh, Library of Congress digitized Persian text
sources.note: Printed page 3, final prose lines: title سراج التواریخ. Direct PDF fetch failed, but exact original URL indexed text read with query site:loc.gov "سراج التواریخ". Normalized modern typesetting, not a facsimile; no claim that OCR reproduces every mark.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Muharabah-i Kabul va Qandahar, catalog 2001287274
sources.note: World Digital Library catalog summary identifies Fayz Muhammad and translates his Siraj al-Tawarikh as Lamp of history. Original indexed catalog fully read; direct fetch 403. This source supplies translation only, not an Afghan place of printing for the cataloged Indian book.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Siraj al-aqaid: hissah-i avval, catalog 00313380
sources.note: Original catalog indexed text read: Persian elementary Islamic education textbook for Afghanistan, Abd al-Rabb Khan, Lahore, circa 1913?, 28 pages; approval note and third-year elementary designation. Uncertain imprint remains explicit.

sources.title: Nancy Hatch Dupree, Cooking iv. In Afghanistan, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 1993
sources.note: Afghanistan section only. Original indexed article and original generated-PDF excerpt checked for hospitality, tea, bread and thanksgiving food. All sections/PDF variants are one work for budget purposes. Describes late twentieth-century practice, not timeless universality.

sources.title: Turquoise Mountain, Rebuilding the Old City
sources.note: First-party restoration report, original indexed full text and direct extraction read. Garbage lowering, courtyard woodwork, library, school conversion and 2013 UNESCO award. Undated webpage; no claim that each facility remains unchanged in 2026.

sources.title: Art Gallery of New South Wales, Journey of the Treasures
sources.note: Direct full exhibition text with interviews, chapters 3 to 5. Museum staff dispersed/hid collections, 2003 public announcement and 2004 authentication. Do not repeat inconsistent 1988/Soviet withdrawal date or disputed seven-key legend.

sources.title: National Gallery of Art, Afghanistan: Hidden Treasures exhibition announcement, 2007/2008
sources.note: Original indexed PDF opening/photo caption read: six Tillya Tepe graves discovered 1978, collapsible first-century CE gold crown for transport. Direct PDF extraction failed.

sources.title: WHO EMRO, Saving lives with mobile health services in Afghanistan, August 2015
sources.note: Original WHO indexed article and WHO archive reproduction at /news/Uncategorised/Page-9-10.html read. Dr Aziza, Nasaji-Bagrami, SHRDO mobile clinic for 450 families. Direct article fetch failed. Archive and USAID PDF reproduction count as same work.

sources.title: Fatima Shahryar, Clean water and school supplies, UNICEF, July 17, 2025
sources.note: Original indexed full report read: Malik Sheer Ahmed school, six-year-old Malika; new toilets, indoor handwashing; nine Logar schools improved. Dated observed project, not countrywide completion.

sources.title: Fatima Shahryar, Water on tap! UNICEF, July 21, 2025
sources.note: Original indexed full report read. Qafila Bashi, Bamyan: Safoora, Zahra and Abdul Ahad; reservoir for 130 households, taps each shared by four or five families, four-kilometre stream trip.

sources.title: UN Women, Women in Afghanistan: From almost everywhere to almost nowhere, August 2023
sources.note: Original indexed report read: 2004 constitution and 2021 women parliamentarians. Used for former constitutional rights, not their current enforcement.

sources.title: UNESCO, Five years on: education for Afghan girls and women, August 11, 2026
sources.note: Direct full text read; updated August 19, 2026. Estimated 2.4 million girls excluded from secondary education, nearly one million enrolled in 2021, community alternatives. Last phase through calendar 2026 is display coverage, not a forecast.

proposedOverrides.name: Afghanistan
proposedOverrides.summary: A country formed from a Durrani inheritance, with changing governments and enduring communities.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One country-history card with ten explicitly separated phases; no additional ID associations. Remove the imported narrow Islamic State of Afghanistan alias from the general record.
batchIdentityNotes.mapInterval: 1783 to open-ended; last decoded geometry ends 2020
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1783 bbox 57.314,28.112,74.429,39.831; 1800 bbox 57.314,28.112,79.933,39.831; from1815 later bbox60.414,29.356,74.735,38.372. Early outlines are broad imperial snapshots; 1960 to1994 one feature spans multiple regimes.
batchIdentityNotes.phaseLimit: 2027 exclusive bound means display coverage through 2026, not a predicted political endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.evidenceLimit: One general country narrative does not associate Islamic State, Islamic Republic and Islamic Emirate as interchangeable regimes. Earlier ancient finds are explicitly retrospective modern discoveries.
